title: Factors affecting natural resources in Ethiopia
competency: State major human activities affecting the natural resources in Ethiopia.

keywords.def: The strain a rising number of people puts on land and resources.
Moving a group of people to a new place or settlement to live in.
Keeping cattle on a piece of land for too long, so the grass is destroyed.
An increasing number of people living in towns and cities.
Growing trees together with crops or animals on farmland.

en.text: Ethiopia has rich resources: land, fertile soil, good climate, water, wildlife, vegetation and minerals. Four factors affect them: population pressure, resettlement, agricultural expansion and rapid urbanization. A rising population makes waste, pressures farmland, and causes pollution and loss of biodiversity. Resettlement moves people to new places, often clearing forests.

screens.title: Twice the people, same land
screens.ask: A district's population doubles, but its land stays the same. What is likely to happen?
opts: More forests are cleared for farms and fuel
screens.after: More people need more farmland, fuel and water. This puts pressure on natural resources.

screens.title: 3.4 Factors affecting natural resources in Ethiopia
paras: Ethiopia is gifted with land, fertile soil, a favorable climate, water, wildlife, vegetation and minerals.
Many of these are not well identified, managed or fully used.
Four connected factors affect them: population pressure, resettlement, agricultural expansion and rapid urbanization.

screens.title: Population pressure
paras: Population is a vital resource and the most important means for development.
But it is also the major factor for natural resource degradation.
A rising population produces waste, pressures arable land, loses biodiversity and pollutes air and water.
It also causes loss of soil fertility, overgrazing and migration of wildlife.

screens.title: Resettlement
paras: Resettlement moves a group of people to a new place to live.
Its aim was to give households productive farmland and food self-sufficiency.
But settlers often cleared dense forests.
This caused deforestation, land degradation and other environmental problems.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The strain a rising number of people puts on land and resources.
Moving a group of people to a new place or settlement to live in.
Keeping cattle on a piece of land for too long, so the grass is destroyed.

screens.text: Which four factors affect natural resources in Ethiopia? Tap all.
screens.why: These four are listed in the book. Agro forestry is a way to conserve resources.

screens.text: Rapid increasing of population number does not affect natural resources.
screens.why: Population is the major factor for natural resource degradation.
screens.clue: Think of waste, farmland and pollution.

screens.ask: The process of moving a group of people to a new place to live is known as ___.
screens.why: This is the book's definition of resettlement.

screens.text: Resettlement aimed to help farmers. Why did it still harm the environment?
opts: Settlers cleared dense forests to make farmland
It moved people into cities only
screens.ans: Settlers cleared dense forests to make farmland
screens.why: The book says resettlement usually took place by clearing natural vegetation in dense forests. This caused deforestation and land degradation.
screens.clue: How did settlers get their new farmland?

en.text: Agricultural expansion changes non-arable land, like forest, into farmland. It causes deforestation, and chemical fertilizers and pesticides pollute soil, air and water. Rapid urbanization is people moving from rural areas to towns. Unplanned city growth, roads and buildings cause deforestation, land degradation and quarrying of sand and gravel.

screens.title: Moving to town
screens.ask: Why do many young people move from rural villages to Addis Ababa or Hawassa?
opts: To find jobs, education and services
screens.after: People migrate to towns for better livelihoods, jobs, education and services. This growth of towns is urbanization.

screens.title: Agricultural expansion
paras: Agricultural expansion is the conversion of non-arable land to arable land, such as forest to farmland.
Agriculture is the backbone of Ethiopia's economy. More than 80% of people work in it.
But it is a major cause of pollution and affects natural resources.
table: Chemical fertilizers and pesticides contaminate living things, soil, air and water
Large horticulture and floriculture farms use many chemicals

screens.title: Rapid urbanization
paras: Rapid urbanization is people shifting from rural to urban areas.
People migrate for better livelihoods, jobs, education and other services.
Cities grow fast and unplanned. Schools, roads, houses and industries replace forests.
This causes land degradation, deforestation and quarrying of sand and gravel.

screens.title: Key words
defs: An increasing number of people living in towns and cities.

screens.ask: ___ is the conversion of non-arable land to arable land.
screens.clue: It is about farming spreading to new land.

screens.text: Chemical fertilizers used in agriculture are major sources of water pollution.
screens.why: Fertilizers and pesticides contaminate soil, air and water.
screens.clue: Where does rain wash the chemicals?

screens.text: Agricultural expansion does not affect natural resources.
screens.why: It causes deforestation and chemical pollution.
screens.clue: What happens to forests when farms grow?

screens.text: Which is an effect of rapid urbanization on natural resources?
opts: Deforestation and quarrying of sand and gravel
screens.ans: Deforestation and quarrying of sand and gravel
screens.why: Building towns clears trees and digs sand, gravel and stone.

screens.text: A new flower farm opens near Lake Ziway. What risk does the book warn about?
opts: Its chemicals may pollute soil, air and water
It has no effect on the lake
screens.ans: Its chemicals may pollute soil, air and water
screens.why: The book says large floriculture farms use many chemicals that pollute soil, air and water quality.
screens.clue: What do large flower farms use a lot of?

en.text: Ethiopia plants trees and runs soil and water conservation campaigns. The main conservation methods are agro forestry, social forestry, and growing towns upward instead of outward. Deforestation destroys resources; reforestation and agro forestry protect them.

screens.title: Saving the hillside
screens.ask: What can a community do to stop soil washing away on a hillside?
opts: Let cattle graze there all year
screens.after: Planting trees and soil and water conservation protect the land. The government runs campaigns for both.

screens.title: Methods of conserving natural resources
paras: The Ethiopian government runs tree planting programs and soil and water conservation campaigns.
The major methods of conserving natural resources are:

screens.title: Key words
defs: Growing trees together with crops or animals on farmland.

screens.text: Which one is NOT a method of conserving natural resources?
screens.why: Deforestation removes trees. The others protect resources.

screens.text: Which factor is NOT a cause of deforestation?
screens.why: Agro forestry is a conservation method.

screens.text: Why does building cities upward help conserve resources?
opts: It uses less land, so fewer forests and farms are cleared
screens.ans: It uses less land, so fewer forests and farms are cleared
screens.why: Tall buildings hold more people on less land.
screens.clue: Compare one tall building with many small ones.

screens.title: Harm or conserve?
screens.why: Conservation adds trees and protects soil; the four factors remove them.
screens.clue: Does it add trees and protect soil, or remove them?

items.text: What are the effects of the destruction of natural resources? Tap all.
items.why: These are the consequences listed under population pressure. Destruction lowers soil fertility.

items.text: How does agricultural expansion affect natural resources?
opts: It clears forests and its chemicals pollute soil, air and water
items.ans: It clears forests and its chemicals pollute soil, air and water
items.why: Forest is converted to farmland; fertilizers and pesticides contaminate the environment.

items.text: What do you mean by resettlement?
opts: Moving a group of people to a new place to live
items.ans: Moving a group of people to a new place to live

items.text: How does rapid urbanization affect natural resources?
opts: Unplanned growth clears forests and digs sand and gravel
items.ans: Unplanned growth clears forests and digs sand and gravel
items.why: Roads, houses and industries cause deforestation, land degradation and quarrying.
items.clue: What do growing towns need land and materials for?

test.text: Which is one of the four factors affecting natural resources in Ethiopia?
test.why: The four factors are population pressure, resettlement, agricultural expansion and rapid urbanization.

test.ask: The permanent removal of trees is called ___.

test.text: More than what percentage of Ethiopians work in agriculture, according to the book?
Agro forestry is a cause of deforestation.
test.why: Agro forestry is a conservation method.

test.text: People move from villages to towns, and the town spreads over forest land. Which two factors are at work?
test.why: Rural-urban migration is urbanization; spreading over forest causes deforestation.
